Extract many layers for an area of interest

Source: R/extract.R
extract_layers.Rd

Extracts data layers on a template raster (such as NAT_DATA's national layers on the national 1 km template) for an area of interest (AOI): each layer is read as an rij matrix (read_rij_matrix()), clipped to the AOI (clip_rij_matrix()) and rebuilt as rasters on the AOI raster's extent (rij_matrix_to_raster()), then returned or, with output_dir, written to GeoTIFF files (write_rasters()). The AOI's cells are worked out once for all layers, and everything that can be checked without extracting is checked before the first layer is read.

Usage

extract_layers(
  layers,
  aoi_raster,
  template,
  output_dir = NULL,
  prefix = "",
  datatype = NULL,
  round_int = TRUE,
  multiband = FALSE,
  drop_empty = TRUE,
  overwrite = TRUE,
  progress = NULL,
  path_column = "path"
)

Arguments

layers

The layers to extract, either:

  • a character vector of file paths: GeoTIFFs on the template's grid, or .rds files holding rij matrices built on the template (such as NAT_DATA's species layers); or

  • a data frame with one row per layer and a column of file paths, named by path_column (path by default), and optionally any of these columns, each overriding the matching argument for its layer (NA uses the argument):

    • prefix: put before the layer's file names ("" for none);

    • datatype: the data type of the layer's files;

    • subdir: the subfolder of output_dir the layer's files go in (NA or "" for output_dir itself); it may hold path separators;

    • format: what the file holds, "auto", "raster" or "rij", as in read_rij_matrix()'s type; NA is "auto", which decides by extension (.tif and .tiff are rasters, .rds an rij matrix).

Other columns are ignored, so a layer catalogue can be passed with its own columns kept, such as the one read_natdata_metadata() returns (with path_column = "file"). A layer may appear more than once (for example written to two subfolders).

aoi_raster

The AOI as a raster: a SpatRaster with one layer, or a path to a raster file, on the template's grid (same CRS, resolution and cell origin), as in clip_rij_matrix(). Every cell that is not NA is in the AOI, whatever its value. Its extent sets the output's extent: the cropped raster rasterize_aoi() returns, or the template's full extent (to extract national rasters for every cell of the template).

template

The template raster the layers are on: a SpatRaster with one layer and a CRS, or a path to a raster file. Only which of its cells have data (are not NA) is used, not its values.

output_dir

NULL (the default) returns the rasters in memory and writes nothing; a single folder path writes them to files there (created if needed) instead. The arguments below output_dir, except drop_empty and progress, are used only when writing.

prefix

A single string put before each file name, for layers with no prefix in layers. "" (the default) adds none. A path separator in it puts the files in a subfolder, as in write_rasters().

datatype

The data type of the written files, for layers with no datatype in layers: one of terra's types ("INT1U", "INT2U", "INT2S", "INT4U", "INT4S", "INT8U", "INT8S", "FLT4S" or "FLT8S"). NULL (the default) uses the data type of the layer's raster file. A layer with none of these (such as an .rds rij matrix, which has no stored data type) has its type inferred from each file's extracted values when it is written, as write_raster_file() does, with a message naming it.

round_int

A single logical, passed to write_rasters(): TRUE (the default) rounds values to whole numbers, halves away from zero, before writing them as an integer type; FALSE lets terra cut the decimals off. Float types are never rounded.

multiband

A single logical: FALSE (the default) writes one file per feature (row of the layer's rij matrix), <output_dir>/<subdir>/<prefix><feature>.tif; TRUE writes one multi-band file per layer, one band per feature, named after the layer's file: <output_dir>/<subdir>/<prefix><file name without extension>.tif (as the opportunity-screening-toolkit names them).

drop_empty

A single logical: TRUE (the default) drops the features with no values in the AOI (every value 0 or NA), as clip_rij_matrix() does, and skips a layer left with none, naming them in a message; FALSE keeps every feature, so a feature absent from the AOI gives a raster of 0s.

overwrite

A single logical, passed to write_rasters(): TRUE (the default) replaces existing files; FALSE stops with an error if an output file exists.

progress

NULL (the default), or a function called before each layer is extracted as progress(i, n, layer): i is the layer's number, n the number of layers and layer its path. Use it to report progress, for example in a Shiny app or a log.

path_column

A single string: the name of the column of layers that holds the layers' file paths, when layers is a data frame. The default, "path", is constechr's own column name; use "file" for the catalogue from read_natdata_metadata(), whose path column is each layer's folder. Not used when layers is a vector of paths.

Value

Without output_dir, a list of SpatRasters held in memory, one per layer with features left after clipping, in the order of layers, named after the layer's file name without its extension, with repeated names made unique by make.unique() (rij, rij.1; see Method); each has one layer per feature, named after it. Layers that were skipped are left out, so the list can be empty.

With output_dir, the paths of the files written, invisibly: a character vector in the order written, named after the feature for one file per feature, or after the layer's file name without its extension for a multi-band file.

Method

  • AOI cells: the cells of aoi_raster that are not NA, where the template has data, matched by position on the shared grid as in clip_rij_matrix(). They are worked out once and used for every layer; the template is read in blocks of rows, so a national template is not held in memory whole.

  • Reading (read_rij_matrix()): a raster layer must be on the template's grid (no resampling; use align_raster() first) and is converted with prioritizr::rij_matrix(); an .rds file is read as it is and must have one column per template cell with data. A one-layer raster file's feature is named after the file (without its extension), a multi-layer file's after its layers, and an rij matrix's after its rows.

  • Clipping (clip_rij_matrix()): the layer's columns in the AOI are kept. With drop_empty = TRUE, a feature is kept if at least one of its values in the AOI is neither 0 nor NA.

  • Rasters (rij_matrix_to_raster()): one layer per feature, on the template's grid cropped to aoi_raster's extent (cut to the template where it reaches past its edge): the feature's values in the AOI cells with template data, 0 where it has none, NA elsewhere. Values are kept as they are (doubles, not rounded, no areas).

  • Names in memory: without output_dir, each raster is named after its layer's file name without its extension. Repeated names (layers with the same file name in different folders, or a layer given twice) are made unique with make.unique(), in the order of layers, among the layers that are not skipped: the first keeps the name and later ones get .1, .2 and so on (rij, rij.1). Names that do not repeat are unchanged. Written files are named by feature, not by these names.

  • Writing (write_rasters()), with output_dir: to <output_dir>/<subdir>/<prefix><feature>.tif, or with multiband = TRUE <output_dir>/<subdir>/<prefix><file name without extension>.tif. Each layer's prefix, datatype and subdir come from layers, else from the arguments; the data type, else, from the layer's raster file, else (such as for an .rds rij matrix) it is inferred from each file's extracted values as in write_raster_file() (ADR 0027): the smallest integer type that holds whole numbers without its NoData value, else "FLT4S", with a message naming it. With round_int = TRUE, values are rounded halves away from zero before an integer type.

  • Checks first: before any layer is read, the layer files must exist, their type must be known, raster layers must open on the template's grid, and, when writing, every data type given must be valid, every prefix and subfolder allowed, and the files that can be named without reading the layers (raster layers' features, and multi-band files) must be distinct (ignoring case), must not be a layer's input file and, with overwrite = FALSE, must not exist. The files of an .rds layer's features are checked the same way when it is written. If a layer still fails (for example an .rds file that does not hold an rij matrix), the error names the layer, and the files of the layers before it are kept.

  • Memory: layers are extracted one at a time, and memory is freed (gc()) after each one, since some national rij matrices are very large.

Method choices are recorded in ADRs 0015 and 0016, and those of the functions it calls in ADRs 0011 to 0014. With layers from read_natdata_metadata(), path_column = "file" and output_dir as <project>/tifs, it writes the same files as wtw-data-prep2's natdata(). Intended changes from that code: everything that can be checked is checked before extracting, dropped features and skipped layers are named in messages, and an error names the layer.

See also

rasterize_aoi() to make aoi_raster; read_natdata_metadata() and natdata_template() for NAT_DATA's layers and template.

Other rij: clip_rij_matrix(), read_rij_matrix(), rij_matrix_to_raster()

Examples

template <- system.file("extdata", "template.tif", package = "constechr")
rij <- system.file("extdata", "rij.rds", package = "constechr")
aoi <- system.file("extdata", "aoi.gpkg", package = "constechr")

# The AOI's cells on the template: a 3 x 3 block, cells 34 to 56
aoi_raster <- rasterize_aoi(aoi, template, cells = "touches")

# In memory: one SpatRaster per layer, here rij.rds's features sp_a and
# cover (sp_b has no values in the AOI, so it is dropped)
x <- extract_layers(rij, aoi_raster, template)
#> Dropped 1 row of /__w/_temp/Library/constechr/extdata/rij.rds with no values in
#> the AOI: "sp_b".
names(x)
#> [1] "rij"
x$rij
#> class       : SpatRaster
#> size        : 3, 3, 2  (nrow, ncol, nlyr)
#> resolution  : 1000, 1000  (x, y)
#> extent      : 1003000, 1006000, 604000, 607000  (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax)
#> coord. ref. : Canada_Albers_WGS_1984
#> source(s)   : memory
#> names       : sp_a, cover
#> min values  :    0,     0
#> max values  :    1,   1.6

# Written: one file per feature, T_sp_a.tif and T_cover.tif, in a
# "species" subfolder, as INT1U (without a datatype, it would be inferred
# from the values, with a message); cover's 1.6 is rounded to 2.
layers <- data.frame(
  path = rij, prefix = "T_", datatype = "INT1U", subdir = "species"
)
output_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "extracted")
paths <- extract_layers(
  layers, aoi_raster, template,
  output_dir = output_dir
)
#> Dropped 1 row of /__w/_temp/Library/constechr/extdata/rij.rds with no values in
#> the AOI: "sp_b".
basename(paths)
#> [1] "T_sp_a.tif"  "T_cover.tif"
terra::values(terra::rast(paths[["cover"]]), mat = FALSE)
#> [1] 0 0 0 0 2 0 0 0 0

# One multi-band file per layer instead, named after the layer's file
paths <- extract_layers(
  rij, aoi_raster, template,
  output_dir = output_dir, datatype = "FLT4S", multiband = TRUE
)
#> Dropped 1 row of /__w/_temp/Library/constechr/extdata/rij.rds with no values in
#> the AOI: "sp_b".
basename(paths)
#> [1] "rij.tif"

# A GeoTIFF on the template too (needs prioritizr), with progress
if (requireNamespace("prioritizr", quietly = TRUE)) {
  x <- extract_layers(
    c(template, rij), aoi_raster, template,
    progress = function(i, n, layer) {
      message("Layer ", i, " of ", n, ": ", basename(layer))
    }
  )
  names(x)
}
#> Layer 1 of 2: template.tif
#> Layer 2 of 2: rij.rds
#> Dropped 1 row of /__w/_temp/Library/constechr/extdata/rij.rds with no values in
#> the AOI: "sp_b".
#> [1] "template" "rij"     

# A table whose file paths are in another column, such as NAT_DATA's
# catalogue (see read_natdata_metadata())
layers <- data.frame(folder = "species", file = rij, datatype = "INT1U")
paths <- extract_layers(
  layers, aoi_raster, template,
  output_dir = output_dir, path_column = "file"
)
#> Dropped 1 row of /__w/_temp/Library/constechr/extdata/rij.rds with no values in
#> the AOI: "sp_b".
basename(paths)
#> [1] "sp_a.tif"  "cover.tif"
